subsections.title: Abilities
text: Many units have core abilities listed on their datasheets, and weapon abilities listed in their weapon profiles.

Weapon abilities are presented in square brackets with bold formatting, e.g. [BLAST]. Weapons are often described using a particular ability they have, e.g. [BLAST] weapons are those with the [BLAST] ability.
If a weapon ability is followed by one or more keywords, when making attacks with that weapon, that ability only applies if the target unit has one or more of those keywords.

Example: The [LETHAL HITS: VEHICLE] ability only applies to attacks that target a VEHICLE unit. The [SUSTAINED HITS 1: INFANTRY/BEASTS] ability only applies to attacks that target an INFANTRY/BEASTS unit.

accordions.title: With The 'X' Ability
text: Some rules affect or require you to select a model or unit with a particular ability. When resolving such rules, any numbers following the ability are irrelevant when determining if such rules apply.

Example: If a rule instructs you to select a model from your army with the Deadly Demise ability, you could select a model with the Deadly Demise 1, Deadly Demise D3 or Deadly Demise D6 ability.

subsections.title: Duplicated Abilities
text: Multiple instances of the same core ability or weapon ability are not cumulative, regardless of any numbers or keywords included in them. In such cases, the controlling player must select which instance will apply at any one time. In the case of duplicated weapon abilities, this selection must be made each time that unit makes attacks, in the Select Weapons step.

• Multiple instances of core abilities that include a number are duplicated even if that number varies. However, in the case of Scouts, you must select the lowest number not shared by every model in that unit (e.g. if every model in a unit has both Scouts 6" and Scouts 8", you could select Scouts 8" as it is shared by every model, but if a unit contains one model with Scouts 6" and five with Scouts 8", you must select Scouts 6").

• Multiple instances of weapon abilities that include a number (e.g. [SUSTAINED HITS 1]) are duplicated even if that number varies (e.g. the controlling player would have to select between [SUSTAINED HITS 1] and [SUSTAINED HITS 2]).

• Multiple instances of weapon abilities that include a keyword are duplicated even if that keyword varies (e.g. the controlling player would have to select between [ANTI‑VEHICLE 4+] and [ANTI‑INFANTRY 2+]).

subsections.title: [ANTI]
text: This ability always takes the form [ANTI‑X Y+]. Each time an attack is made with an [ANTI] weapon, if the target unit has the keyword denoted by X, an unmodified wound roll of Y+ is a critical wound.

Example: An attack made with an [ANTI‑VEHICLE 4+] weapon against a VEHICLE unit will result in a critical wound  on an unmodified wound roll of 4+, while an attack made with an [ANTI‑PSYKER 2+] weapon against a PSYKER unit will result in a critical wound  on an unmodified wound roll of 2+.

subsections.title: [ASSAULT]
text: Units containing one or more models with an [ASSAULT] weapon can shoot using assault shooting (10.05).

subsections.title: [BLAST]
text: Each time you gather attack dice for a [BLAST] weapon, add one additional attack dice for every five models that were in the target unit in the Select Targets step (rounding down).

If this ability takes the form [BLAST X], each time you gather attack dice for such a weapon, add X additional attack dice for every five models that were in the target unit in the Select Targets step (rounding down) instead.

Example: If a [BLAST 2] weapon with an A characteristic of 3 targets a unit containing 12 models, you would gather four additional attack dice for that weapon (for a total of seven for that weapon).

subsections.title: [CLEAVE]
text: This ability always takes the form [CLEAVE X]. Each time you gather attack dice for a [CLEAVE] weapon, if you only selected one target for all of that weapon’s attacks, add X additional attack dice for every five models that were in the target unit in the Select Targets step (rounding down).

Example: If a [CLEAVE 1] weapon with an A characteristic of 3 targets one unit containing 16 models, you would gather three additional attack dice for that weapon (for a total of six for that weapon).

subsections.title: [CLOSE-QUARTERS]
text: Units containing one or more models with a [CLOSE‑QUARTERS] weapon can shoot using close‑quarters shooting (10.06).
When using another shooting type, for each model in that unit (excluding MONSTER/VEHICLE models), you can only select one of the following to make attacks with:
• One or more of its [CLOSE‑QUARTERS] weapons.
• One or more of its other ranged weapons.

subsections.title: Deadly Demise
text: This ability always takes the form Deadly Demise X. Each time a model with this ability is destroyed, after the units embarked within it (if any) have made their emergency disembark moves, roll one D6. On a 6, that model suffers a deadly demise; each unit within 6" of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by X (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6").

subsections.title: Deep Strike
text: Each time this unit makes an ingress move (20.04), if every model in this unit has this ability, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 8" horizontally from all enemy units, even if that is within your opponent’s deployment zone.

subsections.title: [DEVASTATING WOUNDS]
text: Each time an attack made with a [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] weapon results in a critical wound, the attack sequence for that attack ends and the target unit suffers a number of mortal wounds equal to the D characteristic of that weapon. These are inflicted after resolving any normal damage inflicted by those attacks.
Mortal wounds inflicted by [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] weapons can damage a maximum of one model for each critical wound; any remaining mortal wounds inflicted by that attack are lost.

Example: An attack made with a [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] weapon with a D characteristic of 3 results in a critical wound against an Intercessor Squad, so inflicts 3 mortal wounds. The first 2 mortal wounds are sufficient to destroy 1 Intercessor model, so the remaining mortal wound is lost.

subsections.title: [EXTRA ATTACKS]
text: Each time a unit containing one or more models with an [EXTRA ATTACKS] weapon fights, those models will make attacks with those weapons in addition to any others. In the Select Weapons step (04.01), for each of those models, you must select:
• All of that model’s [EXTRA ATTACKS] weapons.
• One of that model’s other melee weapons, if possible.

accordions.title: Only [EXTRA ATTACKS] weapons
text: If a unit has [Extra Attacks] weapons, it does not need to select weapons without the [Extra Attacks] ability in order to make attacks with those [Extra Attacks] weapons.

subsections.title: Feel No Pain
text: This ability always takes the form Feel No Pain X+. Each time a model with this ability would lose a wound, roll one D6: on an X+, that wound is not lost.

subsections.title: Fights First
text: While every model in a unit has this ability, that unit is a Fights First unit.
See the Resolve Fights First Combats step in the Fight phase (12.04).

subsections.title: Firing Deck
text: This ability always takes the form Firing Deck X. In your Shooting phase, each time this TRANSPORT is selected to shoot, if one or more units are embarked within it, resolve the following sequence:
1. Select up to X models embarked within this TRANSPORT (excluding models whose units have already been selected to shoot this phase).
2. For each selected model, select one of its ranged weapons (excluding [ONE SHOT] weapons).
3. Until this TRANSPORT has resolved all of its attacks, it has all of those selected weapons in addition to its other weapons.
4. Until the end of the turn, units embarked within this TRANSPORT are not eligible to shoot.

subsections.title: [HAZARDOUS]
text: Each time a unit is selected to shoot or selected to fight, after that unit has resolved all of its attacks, make a number of hazard rolls (06.03) for that unit equal to the number of [HAZARDOUS] weapons you selected in the Select Weapons step.

subsections.title: [HEAVY]
text: In your Shooting phase, each time an attack is made with a [HEAVY] weapon, add 1 to the hit roll if all of the following apply to the attacking unit:
• That unit is unengaged.
• That unit was not set up on the battlefield this turn.
• No model in that unit has moved moret han 3" this turn.

subsections.title: Hover
text: Each time this unit takes to the skies (21.03), do not subtract 2" from the maximum distance.

subsections.title: [IGNORES COVER]
text: Each time an attack is made with an [IGNORES COVER] weapon, the target cannot have the benefit of cover against that attack (13.08), including from rules that give a model or unit the benefit of cover (e.g. Stealth).

subsections.title: [INDIRECT FIRE]
text: Units containing one or more models with an [INDIRECT FIRE] weapon can shoot using indirect shooting (10.07).

subsections.title: Infiltrators
text: During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 8" horizontally from your opponent’s deployment zone and all enemy units.

subsections.title: [LANCE]
text: Each time an attack is made with a [LANCE] weapon, if the attacking model’s unit made a charge move this turn, add 1 to the wound roll.

subsections.title: Leader
text: Before the battle, in the Muster Armies step, for each leader and support unit in your army, you can select one friendly bodyguard unit that unit can lead. That unit will then lead that bodyguard unit for the battle and form an attached unit with it.
Unless otherwise stated, each bodyguard unit can only have one leader unit and one support unit attached to it.
See Attached Units (19)

subsections.title: [LETHAL HITS]
text: Each time an attack made with a [LETHAL HITS] weapon results in a critical hit, you can choose for that attack to automatically wound the target.

Designer’s Note: Choosing to automatically wound the target means that no wound roll is made for that attack. You may decide against this, as it means that attack cannot result in a critical wound and so cannot trigger other abilities such as [DEVASTATING WOUNDS].

subsections.title: Lone Operative
text: Unless part of an attached unit, this unit is not visible to enemy models unless they are within 12" of this unit, and it cannot be targeted by [INDIRECT FIRE] weapons unless the attacking model is within 12" of this unit.

If this ability takes the form Lone Operative X", unless part of an attached unit, this unit is not visible to enemy models unless they are within X" of this unit, and it cannot be targeted by [INDIRECT FIRE] weapons unless the attacking model is within X" of this unit.

accordions.title: Attached units and Lone Operative
text: If all models in an attached unit have Lone Operative, that unit will benefit from Lone Operative.
If a unit has Lone Operative, but models in that unit have different range values for Lone Operative, the highest value amongst that unit's models on the battlefield is applied to the whole unit.
If an attached unit below starting strength only contains models with Lone Operative, Lone Operative becomes active again.
Example: A Character with Lone Operative is attached to a bodyguard unit that has Lone Operative 15". Lone Operative 15" is therefore used for the whole unit.

Example: A Character with Lone Operative is attached to a bodyguard unit that does not have Lone Operative. Once all of the bodyguard models have been destroyed and only the Character remains, the Character's Lone Operative becomes active again.

subsections.title: [MELTA]
text: This ability always takes the form [MELTA X]. Each time a model makes an attack with a [MELTA] weapon, if the target unit was within half range of that weapon in the Select Targets step, until the attacking unit’s attacks have been resolved, add X to that weapon’s D characteristic.
Example: A model targets a unit that is within half range of a [MELTA 2] weapon with a D characteristic of D6. While resolving those attacks, that weapon has a D characteristic of D6+2

subsections.title: [ONE SHOT]
text: Each weapon with this ability can only be selected to make attacks with once per battle.
If a destroyed model is returned to a unit, all of its [ONE SHOT] weapons that have already been selected to make attacks with during the battle cannot be selected to make attacks with again.
If a new unit is added to an army, all [ONE SHOT] weapons in that unit can be selected to make attacks with once per battle.

accordions.title: Multiple [ONE SHOT] Weapons
text: If a model is equipped with more than one of the same weapon with the [ONE SHOT] ability (e.g. 2 hunter-killer missiles), that model can shoot with each of those weapons once per battle.

subsections.title: [PISTOL]
text: [PISTOL] and [CLOSE‑QUARTERS] are identical for all rules purposes. See [CLOSE‑QUARTERS].

Designer’s Note: [PISTOL] is a pre-existing ability that will be superseded by [CLOSE-QUARTERS] as this edition of Warhammer 40,000 progresses. Both are functionally the same, but the latter is a more suitable term for weapons that function in this way.

subsections.title: [PRECISION]
text: While resolving attacks made with one or more [PRECISION] weapons, at the start of the Allocation Order step (05.03), if the target unit contains one or more CHARACTER models visible to one or more of the attacking models, the active player can select one allocation group that contains one of those visible CHARACTER models. If they do, until those attacks are resolved, or until that CHARACTER group is destroyed (whichever happens first), that CHARACTER group is the current allocation group.

accordions.title: Precision and Devastating Wounds
text: Mortal Wounds inflicted by a [PRECISION] attack with the [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] ability are first applied to the CHARACTER group that was selected for those [PRECISION] attacks (if that group is not already destroyed).

subsections.title: [PSYCHIC]
text: Each time an attack is made with a [PSYCHIC] weapon, you can ignore any or all modifiers to that attack’s BS or WS characteristic and any or all modifiers to the hit roll. Attacks made with [PSYCHIC] weapons are known as psychic attacks (this can be important for the triggering of other rules).

subsections.title: [RAPID FIRE]
text: This ability always takes the form [RAPID FIRE X]. Each time you gather attack dice for a [RAPID FIRE] weapon, add X additional attack dice if the target unit was within half range of that weapon in the Select Targets step.

Example: If a [RAPID FIRE 1] weapon with an A characteristic of 1 targets a unit that is within half range, you would gather one additional attack dice for that weapon (for a total of two for that weapon).

subsections.title: Scouts
text: This ability always takes the form Scouts X". In the Resolve Pre‑battle Abilities step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can do one of the following:
• If that unit is in strategic reserves, you can set up that unit anywhere that is wholly within your deployment zone.
• If that unit is wholly within your deployment zone, it can make a scout move (24.32).

• If that unit is embarked within a DEDICATED TRANSPORT that is wholly within your deployment zone, and if every model embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT has the Scouts ability, that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make a scout move.

subsections.title: Scout Move
text: Eligible If
It is the Resolve Pre-battle Abilities step, and your unit is wholly within your deployment zone.
Effect
Your unit moves as described in Moving (03).
After Moving
Your unit must be more than 8" horizontally from all enemy units.
Maximum Distance
The X" in Scouts X"

subsections.title: Stealth
text: If every model in a unit has this ability, each time a ranged attack targets that unit, that unit has the benefit of cover against that attack (13.08).

subsections.title: Support
text: Before the battle, in the Muster Armies step, for each leader and support unit in your army, you can select one friendly bodyguard unit that unit can lead. That unit will then lead that bodyguard unit for the battle and form an attached unit with it.
Unless otherwise stated, each bodyguard unit can only have one leader unit and one support unit attached to it.
See Attached Units (19).

subsections.title: Super-Heavy Walker
text: Each time a unit with this ability makes a normal, advance or fall-back move:

• Models in that unit can move through models (including MONSTER/VEHICLE models, but excluding TITANIC models) and can move horizontally through sections of terrain features that are 4" or less in height.

• Before moving that unit, you can select for all models in that unit to have the MOBILE keyword until that move ends. If you do, when that move ends, roll one D6: on a 1, that unit is battle-shocked.
Designer’s Note: Gaining the MOBILE keyword for the duration of a move will enable models in that unit to move horizontally through dense terrain features  (13.06).

subsections.title: [SUSTAINED HITS]
text: This ability always takes the form [SUSTAINED HITS X]. Each time an attack made with a [SUSTAINED HITS] weapon results in a critical hit, that attack results in a number of additional hits on the target as denoted by X.

Example: An attack made with a [SUSTAINED HITS 2] weapon results in a critical hit. That attack therefore hits the target three times (once from the critical hit, and twice more from the [SUSTAINED HITS 2] ability).

subsections.title: [TORRENT]
text: Each time an attack is made with a [TORRENT] weapon, that attack automatically hits the target.
[TORRENT] weapons cannot have [INDIRECT FIRE] or [PRECISION].

subsections.title: [TWIN-LINKED]
text: Each time an attack is made with a [TWIN‑LINKED] weapon, you can re‑roll the wound roll.

subsections.title: Damaged
text: This ability always takes the form Damaged X. While a model’s remaining wounds are equal to or less than X, that model is damaged:
• While a model is damaged, that model's attacks have -1 to hit rolls.

faq_screen.question: Can I select a unit to shoot or fight if it doesn't have melee or ranged weapons?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, it just makes no attacks and then the fight type or shoot type is resolved.

faq_screen.question: Can a model be within range of a weapon if it is not visible
faq_screen.answer: Yes

faq_screen.question: Do models destroyed when a unit is out of coherency count for mission objectives?

faq_screen.question: Does my model or unit become engaged while moving through a enemy units engagement range during a move?
faq_screen.answer: No
faq_screen.rationale: Transit does not create lasting engagement; endpoint engagement and overlap remain independently constrained.

faq_screen.question: How many mortals do you take from Hazardous tests for a combined vehicle/monster and Infantry unit
faq_screen.answer: The roll would be all at once and it would be 1 MW per fail
faq_screen.rationale: Hazard damage uses every physical member; mixed Monster/Vehicle and Infantry is one MW per failure.

faq_screen.question: I failed hazard rolls from [Hazardous] weapons, do those mortal wounds have to be allocated to the models with the [Hazardous] weapons?
faq_screen.answer: No, you allocate the mortal wounds to the unit as per Mortal Wounds(06.02). (This represents Bob the guardsmen picking up his fallen squad mates plasma gun or that the twisting power of James the Chaos Sorcerer pulling his followers into the warp.)
faq_screen.rationale: Mortal wounds need not be allocated to a Hazardous weapon bearer.

faq_screen.question: I have a rule that triggers when a mortal wound is allocated to a model, when does this happen?
faq_screen.answer: When you select a model in the Select Model step of Mortal Wounds (06.02).
faq_screen.rationale: Mortal wound allocation trigger belongs to Section06.

faq_screen.question: I have a unit being attacked with weapons that will modify some of their save rolls to be worse then 6 should I make those save rolls?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, because other models in your unit may have Sv's that are better those models you've mentioned, this means that enough save rolls could be allocated to the those models that the rest of the results are not greater then the Sv's of the other models in your unit.
faq_screen.rationale: Mandatory Save rolls belong to Section05.

faq_screen.question: If I have a rule that says my unit can move up to 6" when it makes a pile-in move or consolidation move, does this also mean it changes the maximum distance of those moves to 6"?

faq_screen.rationale: Pile In/Consolidation distance permission cannot override Aircraft Ingress-only restriction.

faq_screen.question: If a rule allows my unit to pile-in or consolidate an extra distance in the Fight phase, when can I use that rule?
faq_screen.answer: For pile-in moves, during the Pile-in step(12.02), and for consolidation moves, during the Consolidate step(12.07) of the Fight phase.
faq_screen.rationale: Fight-step distance permission cannot grant Aircraft a prohibited move.

faq_screen.question: If a rule modifies how far a unit or model can move during a pile-in move or consolidation move does it also change the distance of the target units?
faq_screen.answer: No
faq_screen.rationale: Target range does not change with extra Fight movement; no new Aircraft exception.

faq_screen.question: If a rule says a unit auto passes Desperate Escape tests does that mean it would auto pass the hazard rolls from a desperate escape move?

faq_screen.rationale: Desperate Escape auto-pass semantics are bounded movement dependencies.

faq_screen.question: If a rule says a unit can embark into a Transport in a turn that unit disembarked, does this ignore the core rules restriction on embarking in a turn that unit made a set up move (see 18.02)?

faq_screen.question: If a rule says my unit must make a hazard roll does every model in the unit make a hazard roll?

faq_screen.rationale: Unit Hazard roll cardinality is Section06.

faq_screen.question: If a unit becomes battle-shocked after starting an action does it stop performing that action?
faq_screen.answer: Yes
faq_screen.rationale: Battle-shock interrupts Actions in Section16.

faq_screen.question: If a unit has a rule that allows it to start an action when it is battle-shocked can it also continue doing that action if it becomes battle-shocked after starting an action?
faq_screen.answer: Yes
faq_screen.rationale: Battle-shocked Action permission belongs to Section16.

faq_screen.question: If a unit makes any disembark move in a turn (i.e. Disembark move, Emergency Disembark move etc.) has it disembarked that turn?
faq_screen.answer: Yes.
faq_screen.rationale: Disembark history belongs to Section18.

faq_screen.question: If my unit has taken control of an objective at the end of my movement phase and that unit has as an ability that secures an objective they control, can they secure that objective?
faq_screen.answer: Yes
faq_screen.rationale: Secure Objective timing belongs to mission/Section14.

faq_screen.question: If my unit has the Deadly Demise ability and has an ability that allows it to Fight on Death, how do I resolve this?
faq_screen.answer: Fight on Death rules are resolved before Deadly Demise abilities, meaning that your unit's Deadly Demise will resolve after your unit has fought/at the end of the phase and the relevant models have been removed from the battlefield.
faq_screen.rationale: Authoritative adopted decision: remove relevant FoD models after fight/expiry, then DD measured from pre-destruction position; independent retained casualties remain protected.

faq_screen.question: If my unit has weapons that are identical in characteristics, but some of those weapons have [PRECISION] and those weapons targeted a unit without the character keyword, do I roll all of those weapons together?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, the [PRECISION] ability is not an applicable ability for those attacks as there is no CHARACTER in the target unit for the ability to trigger its rule.
faq_screen.rationale: Precision is not applicable without CHARACTER and permits common gathering then.

faq_screen.question: If the [ANTI] ability on my unit is ANTI-non-Monster/Vehicle does it mean the [ANTI] rule triggers when targeting units that do not have the Monster or Vehicle keyword?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, ANTI-non-(any keyword) will trigger on any unit that does not have the specified keyword.
faq_screen.rationale: ANTI-non keywords match absence of all specified keywords, using exact canonical membership.

faq_screen.question: My rule says that "this units ranged attacks have +1 A", do each of my attacks get an extra attack dice?
faq_screen.answer: No, it increases the A characteristics of the unit's ranged weapons by 1.
faq_screen.rationale: Attack count modifiers belong to Section02/04.

faq_screen.question: The Munitorium Field Manual shows my unit can attach to different units then are on it's datasheet, which do I use?
faq_screen.answer: Use the Munitorium Field Manual.
faq_screen.rationale: MFM eligibility authority is inherited from accepted Section19; constructed Support never certifies a native provider.

faq_screen.question: What does the X" in Lone Operative X" mean?
faq_screen.answer: The X is a placeholder for a number of inches that the ability might appear in a rule with, like Lone Operative 15" where the X has been replaced with 15"
faq_screen.rationale: X denotes a numeric inch parameter; bare Lone Operative uses12 inches.

faq_screen.question: When a move says that a model or unit must move in a way if it is able, can that requirement force the unit to end their move not in coherency?
faq_screen.answer: No, when a model or unit is making a move it must follow requirements while ending that move in coherency
faq_screen.rationale: Movement must still end coherent; Aircraft transit permission does not waive this existing geometry rule.

faq_screen.question: When a rule instructs you to perform a charge outside of the charge phase, do I resolve step 2 and 3 of the Charge step(11.02)?
faq_screen.answer: Yes
faq_screen.rationale: Out-of-phase charge follows ordinary charge steps; Aircraft charge prohibition is unchanged.

faq_screen.question: When checking coherency for my unit can my unit be in multiple groups?
faq_screen.answer: No, it must be in a single contiguous group as per Units and Models (01.02) and What is Coherency in the core rules.
faq_screen.rationale: Contiguous coherency remains a movement prerequisite.

faq_screen.question: When declaring the allocation order of groups in my unit I have more than one non-CHARACTER groups that contain a model with a missing wound, how must I select the order?
faq_screen.answer: Those groups can be selected in an order of your choosing but must be in an order that makes them come before any non-CHARACTER groups that do not contain a model with a missing wound.
faq_screen.rationale: Allocation group order is Section05.

faq_screen.question: When selecting a target unit can the enemy model that is visible to my model and the enemy model that is in range of my model's weapon be different enemy models in the same unit?

faq_screen.question: Can an attached unit be given an Upgrade?

faq_screen.question: Can a unit have both an Upgrade and an enhancement?

faq_screen.question: Are Upgrades enhancements?

faq_screen.question: Are models that are within the boundary of a terrain area, but not on the ground floor of a terrain area (e.g. overhanging parts of FRAME VEHICLES or models on terrain features that are within that terrain area) within that terrain area?

faq_screen.question: Do rules that affect a keyword include multi-word keywords that contain that keyword? For example, would rules that affect Commissar units affect a unit that has the Commissar Graves keyword?

faq_screen.question: After using an ability that increases the CP cost of a stratagem, must my opponent continue to use the selected stratagem at the increased cost if they have the necessary CP available?

faq_screen.question: In what step during the attack sequence do I roll for Feel No Pain?

faq_screen.question: Can an Epic Hero unit form an attached unit with a unit that has an enhancement?

faq_screen.question: While making a move type other than a normal/advance move, can my MONSTER/VEHICLE unit move through friendly units?

faq_screen.question: If I place units in strategic reserves during the battle, can this exceed the 50% of my points limit for the battle restriction as mentioned in Placing Units in Strategic Reserves (20.01)?

faq_screen.question: Does the limit to the combined points value of my units in strategic reserves only apply until the start of the first battle round?
faq_screen.answer: Yes.
faq_screen.rationale: The points restriction is a pre-battle declaration boundary; mandatory deployment and battle re-entry keep distinct owners.

faq_screen.question: After using an ability that increases the CP cost of a stratagem, if my opponent does not have the necessary CP available for the selected stratagem, what happens?

faq_screen.question: Is being within range of a terrain objective the same as being within range of an objective marker?

faq_screen.question: When my unit shoots at another unit, how does it work if some models in the target unit are fully visible to some models in my unit, while others are within a terrain area/not fully visible?
faq_screen.answer: For each attacking model in your unit, determine whether the target unit has the benefit of cover, as described in Terrain and Visibility. In this scenario, the target unit will likely have the benefit of cover against some of the attacking models, but not all. This means that, in an example unit where all attacking models are using the same weapon, when you get to the Resolve Attacks step of the Attack Sequence, you will collect dice for attacks made by models against which the target unit has the benefit of cover separately from the dice for attacks made by models against which the target unit does not have the benefit of cover.
faq_screen.rationale: Cover is evaluated per attacking model; Ignores Cover also defeats Stealth cover.

faq_screen.question: If a stratagem contains a section that carries an additional CP cost (such as the Into the Fray option of Heroic Intervention), is that additional cost considered to be a modifier?

faq_screen.rationale: Optional Stratagem CP cost is Section15.

faq_screen.question: Does vertical movement in a unit that has taken to the skies count towards the distance a model has used for the purposes of [Heavy]?

faq_screen.question: Can I group or allocate a wound to a destroyed model?
faq_screen.answer: No.
faq_screen.rationale: Destroyed models cannot receive new wounds; retained physical presence does not mean living allocation eligibility.

faq_screen.question: My unit has access to a rule that changes the Damage characteristic of an incoming attack to 0. When such an attack is allocated to a model in that unit, is the Damage changed before or after save rolls?
faq_screen.answer: After.
faq_screen.rationale: Zero-damage timing is Section05.

faq_screen.question: Fight On Death (05.04.05) requires models awaiting such an ability to stay on the battlefield until their unit has attacked (or until the end of the phase). How do these models function while this is the case?
faq_screen.answer: Models awaiting a Fight On Death ability are still present on the battlefield for all rules purposes. This includes (but is not limited to) the following regarding such models: They can be measured to by friendly/enemy abilities. They can be considered visible to friendly/enemy models where relevant. They can use their datasheet abilities. They can be targeted by stratagems. Enemy units can still be engaged with them (which may restrict the opposing player's consolidation/pile-In moves made as part of an overrun fight).
faq_screen.rationale: Retained destroyed models are physically present until relevant cleanup; physical presence, living ability availability and selected content are distinct.

faq_screen.question: Can I use the Insane Bravery stratagem on a battle-shocked unit?
faq_screen.answer: No, as a unit's controlling player cannot target that unit with stratagems (01.07).
faq_screen.rationale: Battle-shocked Stratagem target restriction is Section15.

faq_screen.question: Units have all the keywords of all their models, and attached units have all the keywords of all of their component units. How are destroyed models taken into account for these purposes?
faq_screen.answer: These statements are only true so long as the models possessing those keywords remain part of the unit; destroyed models do not contribute their keywords to their prior unit. Example: The Aspiring Sorcerer model in a unit of Rubric Marines is destroyed; as none of the remaining models in the unit possess the PSYKER keyword, that unit is no longer a PSYKER unit.
faq_screen.rationale: Casualties remove keyword contributions; retained physical members follow the adopted retained-presence authority.

faq_screen.question: Do a unit's abilities continue to function while they are embarked within a TRANSPORT?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, within the restrictions specified by the ability itself. Embarked units are Not On The Battlefield (01.02.04), so any ability requiring visibility or measurement to another unit will fail. Example: Azrael is attached to an Intercessor Squad unit and embarked within a TRANSPORT, and that TRANSPORT is making a shooting attack using the Firing Deck ability. While Azrael's Supreme Grand Master ability is still technically active, it will have no effect, as the requirements of the ability are not met (the ability affects 'weapons equipped by models' in Azrael's unit, and for the purposes of Firing Deck, the TRANSPORT itself is equipped with those weapons instead).
faq_screen.rationale: Cargo abilities do not transfer their bearer ownership to transport-equipped Firing Deck weapons.

faq_screen.question: When checking line of sight from one model to another, is this drawn between the bases of those models, or between any part of them?
faq_screen.answer: Line of sight is drawn from any part of the observing model to any part of the model being observed.
faq_screen.rationale: Full model visibility geometry remains inherited; no Aircraft-specific observer exception.

faq_screen.question: If both players have units with the Scouts ability, do they alternate resolving scout moves?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, players alternate resolving any pre-battle rules units from their army may have, starting with the player who will take the first turn.
faq_screen.rationale: Both players alternate pre-battle abilities starting with first turn player.

faq_screen.question: My attack has a rule that means it results in a critical hit on a hit roll of 4+. Does this work when snap shooting?
faq_screen.answer: Unless otherwise stated, no: when snap shooting, each attack only hits on a roll of 6.
faq_screen.rationale: Snap shooting only hits on6; critical modifiers do not waive that condition.

faq_screen.question: My attack has a rule that means it results in a critical hit on a hit roll of 4+, and I would otherwise need a 5+ to hit. Does a 4+ hit?
faq_screen.answer: Yes, except when snap shooting: when snap shooting, each attack only hits on a roll of 6.
faq_screen.rationale: Critical thresholds can bypass ordinary required Hit number except Snap shooting only6. Retain Section04 critical control.

faq_screen.question: When do the effects of a FLYING unit taking to the skies apply?
faq_screen.answer: When that unit is selected to make a normal/advance/fall-back/charge move. Note that for an advance/charge move, this means you must declare that a unit will take to the skies before rolling for that advance/charge move.
faq_screen.rationale: FLY identity supplies Aircraft combat eligibility; Take to the Skies is an optional movement choice and does not create that keyword.

faq_screen.question: If a rule refers to an 'objective marker', does this mean an 'objective'?
faq_screen.answer: Yes (excluding rules in the Core Rules)'.
faq_screen.rationale: Objective marker non-Core terminology remains inherited Section14 qualification.

faq_screen.question: How do modifiers to the charge roll (or to the maximum distance of the charge move, such as Take to the Skies) affect the selection of charge targets?
faq_screen.answer: A charging unit may only select charge targets that are within the maximum distance of their charge roll, including any modifiers. If such a modifier occurs after selecting a charge target and causes that charge target to no longer be within the maximum distance, the charging unit would then select new targets (Target No Longer Eligible Or Viable, 04.03.03). Example: A unit's charge roll is 7", and that unit has a datasheet ability which adds 1 to charge rolls: that charge's maximum distance is 8", so you can select charge targets within 8". Example: A FLYING unit chooses to take to the skies and rolls a charge roll of 9"; that charge's maximum distance is 7" (9" minus the 2" from taking to the skies), so you can select charge targets within 7".
faq_screen.rationale: Modified charge distance changes target range; FLY Aircraft target permission is an additional conjunction.

faq_screen.question: Can a unit be controlling more than one objective at once?
faq_screen.answer: Yes.
faq_screen.rationale: Multiple objective control belongs to Section14.

faq_screen.question: When determining control over an objective, can the same model's OC count towards more than one objective that model is within range of?
faq_screen.answer: Yes.
faq_screen.rationale: Model OC may count to multiple objectives in Section14.

faq_screen.question: If a rule's effect lasts until the end of a specific part of the battle (e.g. until the end of the phase, until the end of the turn), is that rule still in effect at the end of that part of the battle?
faq_screen.answer: Yes. For example, if an ability gave a unit +1 OC until the end of the turn, at the end of the turn, that unit would still have +1 OC. That unit would not have +1 OC at the start of the next turn.
faq_screen.rationale: End-turn effects remain in force through end-turn hooks; this work adds no effect expiration change.

faq_screen.question: When a model overhangs the edge of the battlefield, how does that affect its visibility?
faq_screen.answer: That model's controlling player can draw line of sight from any part of that model that is not overhanging the edge of the battlefield. Their opponent can draw line of sight to any part of that model.
faq_screen.rationale: Asymmetric overhang visibility remains a bounded geometry dependency with no Aircraft exception.

faq_screen.question: When does a model's or unit's ability in an attached unit apply to all models in that unit?
faq_screen.answer: A rule that applies to 'this/that unit' or 'models in this/that unit' applies to all models in an attached unit. Rules that just apply to one model in an attached unit (for example, a rule that grants a model Feel No Pain or Lone Operative) only apply to that model, not to all models in the attached unit.
faq_screen.rationale: Model-specific Lone Operative/FNP does not spread through an attachment; unit-targeted rules may.
